**I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**

Fiscal year 2026 was the most consequential year in the Collaborative's history. We served 1,847 clients across our three core program areas — housing stability, family law, and income maintenance — a 12% increase over 2025. Our staff grew from 14 to 18 full-time equivalents, including two new staff attorneys and a dedicated intake coordinator funded through the State Access to Justice Commission grant. While demand continues to outpace capacity, the investments made this year in technology, outreach, and interpreter services have materially improved both the speed and quality of our services.

The Board approved a FY2027 operating budget of $1.24 million, reflecting continued growth in both public and private funding. We enter the new year with a reserves balance of $86,000, approximately seven weeks of operating expenses. This is below our stated target of three months, and the Board has asked staff to prioritize unrestricted fundraising in the first two quarters of 2027.

**Housing Stability Program**

- Eviction diversion clinics held monthly at the North Harborview Community Center and the Maple Leaf Library. Combined attendance: 412 households.
